goal: Users can run one shared React workbench in Web, macOS, and Windows runtimes through versioned transports while the deterministic Python CLI remains independent.
non_goals: Do not introduce PySide6, PyQt, Electron, or a second desktop component tree.
Do not change parser, validator, compiler, renderer, template, bibliography, or DOCX semantics.
Do not implement final cancellation, streamed progress, diagnostics localization, preview mapping, template behavior, release signing, or installer acceptance assigned to later slices.
Do not introduce autosave, database, accounts, AI, telemetry, dark mode, or public multi-tenant hosting.
expected_evidence: Strict TDD RED for missing frontend workspace, workspace state, transports, Python adapters, Tauri bridge, and CLI isolation contract
Shared Python and TypeScript workspace-state parity fixtures
Vitest and Testing Library coverage for shell, labels, keyboard focus, shortcuts, states, capabilities, responsive panels, and resize behavior
Playwright browser launch and responsive behavior evidence
Python HTTP and sidecar contract tests proving delegation to existing application services and JSON-safe DTOs
Cargo test/check for the Tauri command bridge and sidecar envelope
Frontend build, lint, typecheck, full Python tests, Ruff, pip check, strict OpenSpec, SpecNav entry, CodeGraph, JSON, and whitespace evidence
Task report, dedicated spec review, and dedicated quality review
unsafe_assumptions: Browser and desktop source capabilities can share raw native path DTOs.
React components may call HTTP or Tauri directly.
A generated Tauri config proves sidecar protocol behavior.
Frontend build success proves keyboard, responsive, or parity behavior.
The Python CLI remains independent without an explicit import and distribution test.
stop_condition: Stop if implementation needs edits outside the allowed files, duplicates compiler behavior, exposes browser-native paths, couples shared React code to HTTP/Tauri/Python, introduces a Qt product dependency, or requires signing credentials or release-only host changes.
